title: Tongariro Power Scheme

title: Arapuni Hydro Station
note: Opened 1929; 8 Francis turbines (units 5-6 1938, 7-8 1946; 5-8 replaced 2012-13); 198 MW; 870 GWh a year.

title: Aratiatia Hydro Station
note: Opened 1964; 3 Francis turbines; 78 MW; 335 GWh a year; 13 km downstream of Taupō; rapids releases.

title: Ātiamuri Hydro Station
note: Opened 1958; 4 Francis turbines; 84 MW.

title: Hydro generation: the Waikato Hydro System
note: The nine Waikato River stations; planned upgrades (Ātiamuri 2031-34, Maraetai I 2030-34, Ōhakuri 2029-32).

title: Karāpiro Hydro Station
note: Built 1940-47; 3 Kaplan turbines of 37.5 MW, commissioned 1947-48; 112.5 MW since the upgrade completed Sep 2025 (96 MW before).

title: Maraetai I and II Hydro Station
note: Maraetai I opened 1952, Maraetai II 1970 (begun 1959, paused 1961); 5 Francis turbines and 180 MW each; one shared arch dam.

title: Ōhākurī Hydro Station
note: Opened 1961; 4 Francis turbines (replaced 2011-14); 112 MW; 405 GWh a year; Lake Ōhakuri 12 km².

title: Waipāpa Hydro Station
note: Opened 1961; 3 Kaplan turbines; 51 MW; 240 GWh a year; smallest station on the Waikato River.

title: Whakamaru Hydro Station
note: Built from 1949, operating 1956; 4 Francis turbines, replaced 2017-20; 124 MW; 515 GWh a year.

title: Aviemore Power Station
note: Four 55 MW units, up to 220 MW; generators the largest in NZ by size (rotors nearly 8 m, 210 t); earth and concrete dam; 7 m penstocks; approved October 1962; construction 1962, fully operational 1968; mid-Waitaki scheme with Benmore and Waitaki.

title: Benmore hydro station
note: Six 93 MW units, up to 552 MW (before the July 2026 reassessment); on Lake Benmore, NZ's largest artificial lake; NZ's largest earth dam; approved October 1957 with the Cook Strait cable; built from 1958; lake filled December 1964; first power January 1965.

title: Hydro stations
note: Waitaki hydro scheme: eight stations; Meridian owns and operates Aviemore, Benmore, Waitaki and Ōhau A, B and C; Genesis Energy owns and operates Tekapo A and B. Manapōuri is NZ's largest hydro station.

title: Lake levels
note: Lakes Pūkaki, Ōhau, Ruataniwha, Benmore, Aviemore, Waitaki, Manapōuri and Te Anau; flows in the Waitaki River below Benmore, Aviemore and Waitaki dams; Lakes Te Anau and Manapōuri supply Manapōuri.

title: Manapōuri Power Station
note: Seven 128 MW units; operating maximum 800 MW (consent), 850 MW maximum continuous rating with the second tailrace; cavern about 200 m below Lake Manapōuri (West Arm), Fiordland National Park; built from 1964 by about 1,800 workers over eight years; first power September 1969; fully operational 1972; second tailrace 1998–2002; tailraces to Deep Cove, Doubtful Sound.

title: Ōhau A Power Station
note: Four 66 MW units, up to 264 MW; at the end of the Pūkaki canal where it meets the Ōhau canal; third station of the Upper Waitaki scheme; construction 1971, fully operational 1979; Lake Ruataniwha rowing course.

title: Ōhau B hydro station
note: Four 53 MW units, up to 212 MW; twin of Ōhau C; water from Lake Ruataniwha into the Ōhau C canal; construction 1977, fully operational 1984.

title: Ōhau C Power Station
note: Twin of Ōhau B; four 53 MW units, up to 212 MW; outflow to Lake Benmore; construction 1979, fully operational 1985, the last station of the Waitaki scheme.

title: Waitaki Power Station
note: Seven 15 MW units, up to 105 MW; Depression make-work project, dug by pick and shovel; first two units 1935, three more 1940–49, last two 1952–54; $440–510 million upgrade to 120 MW, due by 2036.

title: About the Waitaki hydro scheme
note: Eight stations from Lake Tekapo to Lake Waitaki, six run by Meridian from Twizel; Waitaki dam begun 1928; Aviemore (1968) completed the mid-Waitaki scheme; Upper Waitaki 1968–85; 1999 Meridian assigned the scheme; 2011 Tekapo A and B sold to Genesis Energy.

title: Increased generation capacity at Waitaki hydro stations (30 July 2026)
note: Maximum operating capacity from 30 July 2026: Benmore 552 → 570 MW, Ōhau B 216 → 220 MW, Ōhau C 212 → 220 MW.

title: Tekapo A Power Station
note: Southern end of Lake Tekapo; begun 1938, interrupted by the war, opened 1951; one unit, vertical Kaplan turbine, 30 MW; turbine destroyed 1986 and replaced; canal to Tekapo B; Meridian to 2011, then Genesis.

title: Tekapo B Power Station
note: Eastern shore of Lake Pūkaki; built 1970–77, before the lake was raised; two Francis units of 80 MW (citing Meridian's Discover the Waitaki Hydro Scheme); Meridian to 2011, then Genesis.

title: Clyde hydro power station
note: On the Clutha River in Central Otago; Lake Dunstan; commissioned 1992; max capacity 464 MW from four turbine generator units; annual output 2,250 GWh; the largest concrete gravity dam in New Zealand; about one million m³ of concrete in the dam and 200,000 m³ in the powerhouse.

title: Roxburgh hydro power station
note: Clutha River, Central Otago; commissioned 1956 and 1962; max capacity 320 MW; annual output 1,750 GWh; eight generators, the first commissioned in 1956; concrete gravity dam; lake of nearly 6 km².

title: Clutha Mata Au Hydro Scheme
note: The scheme name. Roxburgh turbine upgrade: four of eight turbines replaced 2024–2026, the first operational January 2025; +44 GWh a year; commissioned 1956–1962 with eight turbines made in Canada by Dominion Turbines.

title: New turbines at Contact's Roxburgh dam to create more renewable energy (10 June 2024)
note: Commissioned 1956–1962; eight original Canadian-built turbines, the first four installed 1956–57 and the second four 1960–61; four replaced by Voith, first components on site 7 June 2024; +44 GWh a year; 320 MW.

title: Voith completes second turbine upgrade at New Zealand's Roxburgh hydropower station (30 September 2025)
